An improvement over NDC and basic contraction (Barron et al., 2022) designed to constrain long-range street view sequences into a bounded range before position encoding.
It avoids the heavy range compression of close objects that occurs in standard NDC, which fails in scenes with complicated ego-car motions and challenging camera settings.
It provides more details for close object rendering by decoupling the near-field resolution from the far-field bound via the radius parameter $r$.
It is chosen when rendering street views with significant depth variation and ego-motion, where standard NDC artifacts are prominent.
It links to [Unbounded inward-facing scene parameterization](957-unbounded-inward-facing-scene-parameterization.md).
- **Time complexity:** $O(1)$ per point for the parameterization function.
- **Memory complexity:** $O(1)$ auxiliary memory.
NDC fails in these specific ego-vehicle scenarios due to complex motion, making this parameterization necessary.
- **When to use:** Unbounded inward-facing street scenes with ego-motion.
- **When not to use:** Bounded indoor scenes or scenes where NDC is sufficient and stable.
Originated in S-NeRF (2023) for neural radiance fields in street views.
It addresses the failure of Normalized Device Coordinates (NDC) in scenes with complicated ego-car motions and challenging camera settings.
It improves upon the scene parameterization function used in Mip-NeRF 360 (Barron et al., 2022) by introducing the radius parameter $r$.

It is used in conjunction with frustum sampling from Mip-NeRF (Barron et al., 2021), sampling along rays evenly in a log scale to get more points close to the near plane, further enhancing close-object detail.
